title: Revenue Accounting Definition: Fare Part of a Ticket's Trip Spend
content:
**Definition — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The fare part of the trip spend of a ticket is measured by one of three conventions:

1. On a ticket with at least one flown coupon, it is the fare still unflown: the fare collected less the coupon value already flown.
2. On a round-trip ticket with no flown coupon, it is half the fare collected.
3. On any other ticket, it is the whole fare collected.

The fare collected is every fare-collection and add-collect entry on the ticket; the coupon value already flown is every flown-coupon entry on it.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Ticket | Fare collected | Coupon value flown | Fare part |
|---|---|---|---|
| Round trip, outbound flown | 600.00 | 290.00 | 310.00 |
| Round trip, nothing flown, one add-collect of 40.00 on a fare collection of 500.00 | 540.00 | 0 | 270.00 |
| One way, nothing flown | 380.00 | 0 | 380.00 |
| One way with a connection, first segment flown | 380.00 | 170.00 | 210.00 |
